50470091.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to N-terminal His6-tagged BRD2 bromodomain 1 (unknown origin) expressed in competent Escherichia coli BL21(DE3) cells by isothermal titration calorimetry

original_paragraph.Isothermal Titration Calorimetry: ITC experiments were carried out on an ITC200 instrument from MicroCal™. Experiments were conducted at either 15°C, 25°C or 30°C, while stirring at 1000 rpm. Buffers of proteins, peptide and compounds were matched to 20 mM HEPES pH 7.5 at 25°C and 100 mM NaCl. Frozen protein was buffer exchanged as described for the DSF experiments. Each titration comprised 1 initial injection of 0.4 μL lasting 0.8 s, followed by 19 injections of 2 μL lasting 4 s each at 2 min intervals. The initial injection was discarded during data analysis. Peptide Binding: Experiments with the tetra acetylated histone peptide were performed at 15°C. The micro syringe (40 μL) was loaded with a solution of the peptide sample at a concentration of 1-2 mM and injected into the cell (200 μL), occupied by a protein at a concentration of 50-100 μM. Ligand Binding: Experiments with ME against WT, L/A and L/I mutant Brd2 bromodomains were conducted at 25°C. A solution of protein (350-400 μM for WT, 150-200 μM for mutants) was titrated into a solution of compound ME in the cell (15-20 μM). Experiments with 28 were carried at 30°C. A 250 μM solution of 28 as titrated into a 25 μM solution of protein in the cell. The DMSO concentration was adjusted to 2.5 % both in the syringe and in the cell. Data Analysis: All the data was fitted to a single binding site model using the Microcal LLC ITC200 Origin software provided by the manufacturer to yield enthalpies of binding (ΔH) and binding constants (Kₐs). Further thermodynamical parameters were calculated from these values (changes in entropy ΔS, changes in free energy ΔG and dissociation constants (Kdₛ)).

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods: Isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC) experiments were performed on a MicroCal iTC200 instrument (Malvern Instruments, Worcestershire, U.K.) at 25 °C. The protein (10–20 μM) was loaded into the sample cell, and the ligand (100–200 μM) was loaded into the syringe. The buffer used was 20 mM HEPES, 100 mM NaCl, 0.01% Tween 20, pH 7.5. The stirring speed was set to 300 rpm. The titration consisted of 20 injections of 2 μL each, with a 180 s spacing between injections. The data were analyzed using Origin 7.0 software (MicroCal) with a one-site binding model. The reported Kd values are the average of at least two independent experiments. The binding enthalpy (ΔH) was calculated from the integrated heat of each injection. The control experiments were performed by titrating the ligand into buffer alone to correct for the heat of dilution. The data were fitted to a one-site binding model using the MicroCal Origin software. The reported Kd values are the average of at least two independent experiments. The binding enthalpy (ΔH) was calculated from the integrated heat of each injection. The control experiments were performed by titrating the ligand into buffer alone to correct for the heat of dilution. The data were fitted to a one-site binding model using the MicroCal Origin software.

The side chain of His433 switches from an “open” conformation when bound to 1 to a “closed” conformation when bound to 28, engaging in an edge-to-face interaction with 28. All structures show a conserved scaffold binding mode in the K(Ac) pocket.

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods: ITC experiments were performed on a MicroCal iTC200 instrument (Malvern Instruments, Worcestershire, U.K.) at 25 °C. The protein (10–20 μM) was dialyzed against 20 mM HEPES, 100 mM NaCl, 1 mM DTT, pH 7.5, and loaded into the sample cell. The ligand (1–2 mM) was dissolved in the same buffer and loaded into the syringe. The reference cell was filled with buffer. The titration consisted of 20 injections of 2 μL each, with a 120 s spacing between injections. The data were analyzed using Origin 7.0 software (OriginLab, Northampton, MA) with a one-site binding model. The reported Kd values are the average of at least two independent experiments. The thermal stability of the proteins was assessed by DSF as described previously.11

50470082.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to recombinant poly-His-tagged BRD2 bromodomain 1 (unknown origin) by isothermal titration calorimetry

original_paragraph.Isothermal Titration Calorimetry: ITC experiments were carried out on an ITC200 instrument from MicroCal™. Experiments were conducted at either 15°C, 25°C or 30°C, while stirring at 1000 rpm. Buffers of proteins, peptide and compounds were matched to 20 mM HEPES pH 7.5 at 25°C and 100 mM NaCl. Frozen protein was buffer exchanged as described for the DSF experiments. Each titration comprised 1 initial injection of 0.4 μL lasting 0.8 s, followed by 19 injections of 2 μL lasting 4 s each at 2 min intervals. The initial injection was discarded during data analysis. Peptide Binding: Experiments with the tetra acetylated histone peptide were performed at 15°C. The micro syringe (40 μL) was loaded with a solution of the peptide sample at a concentration of 1-2 mM and injected into the cell (200 μL), occupied by a protein at a concentration of 50-100 μM. Ligand Binding: Experiments with ME against WT, L/A and L/I mutant Brd2 bromodomains were conducted at 25°C. A solution of protein (350-400 μM for WT, 150-200 μM for mutants) was titrated into a solution of compound ME in the cell (15-20 μM). Experiments with 28 were carried at 30°C. A 250 μM solution of 28 as titrated into a 25 μM solution of protein in the cell. The DMSO concentration was adjusted to 2.5 % both in the syringe and in the cell. Data Analysis: All the data was fitted to a single binding site model using the Microcal LLC ITC200 Origin software provided by the manufacturer to yield enthalpies of binding (ΔH) and binding constants (Kₐs). Further thermodynamical parameters were calculated from these values (changes in entropy ΔS, changes in free energy ΔG and dissociation constants (Kdₛ)).

50470081.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to recombinant poly-His-tagged BRD2 bromodomain 2 (unknown origin) by isothermal titration calorimetry

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods: Isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC) experiments were performed on a MicroCal iTC200 instrument (Malvern Instruments, Worcestershire, U.K.) at 25 °C. The protein (10–20 μM) was loaded into the sample cell, and the ligand (100–200 μM) was loaded into the syringe. The buffer used was 20 mM HEPES, 100 mM NaCl, 0.01% Tween 20, pH 7.5. The stirring speed was set to 750 rpm. The titration consisted of 20 injections of 2 μL each, with a 120 s spacing between injections. The data were analyzed using Origin 7.0 software (MicroCal) with a one-site binding model. The reported Kd values are the average of at least two independent experiments. The binding enthalpy (ΔH) was calculated from the integrated heat of each injection. The control experiment involved titrating the ligand into buffer alone to correct for the heat of dilution.

assay_conditions.control_method: Titration of ligand into buffer alone to correct for the heat of dilution
